title: Runtime readiness verification and model warmup checks for Private deployment
creator: Connor Wu
description: Objective: Implement a lightweight, deterministic post-deploy verification harness that runs after Terraform completes on Private (VPC) deployments. The harness must validate API readiness, exercise model load and warmup paths, run smoke inference across AZs, and surface failure signals suitable for automated rollback or operator alerting. This ticket covers the engineering work to: (1) wire the harness into the current Terraform modules as a post-apply hook; (2) implement a containerized runner that performs API readiness checks, model load/health probes, KV-cache priming, and synthetic inference smoke/load tests; (3) emit standardized Prometheus/Grafana metrics and structured test results to the console so Console and alerting rules can act; and (4) add an enable/disable flag and sane timeouts so customers can opt out or tune the checks. Rationale: our Private deployments are increasingly used by security-conscious customers who expect deterministic validation after upgrades and initial installs. Current smoke tests are ad-hoc and run manually; we need an automated, auditable, and repeatable post-deploy verification step integrated into IaC.
acceptance_criteria: A post-apply hook is added to the terraform private deployment module that invokes the verification runner (toggleable via module variable 'post_deploy_checks_enabled')
The runner performs an API readiness probe (health endpoints + authentication token validation) against the customer control plane and returns non-0 exit codes on failure

The runner exercises model load paths for at least two representative model types (a small encoder-only embeddings model and a decoder generative model) and validates successful weight load and KV-cache allocation
Synthetic inference smoke tests return stable outputs and meet latency SLOs (p95 < configured threshold) for single-request paths; failures are captured and emitted as structured JSON
A basic concurrent model-load test (3 parallel cold-starts) completes without OOM and produces the expected model-serving metrics (model_loaded_count, kernel_init_time)
Runner emits Prometheus metrics and pushes a run-level JSON result to the deployment console S3 bucket (or customer-specified artifact store) with timestamps and git-sha of infra code
Documentation and runbook added to Confluence with troubleshooting steps, failure modes, and recommended timeouts.
runbook_steps: 1) After terraform apply completes, terraform calls the 'post_deploy_checks' null_resource local-exec which runs the containerized runner image with environment variables from terraform outputs (api_url, admin_token, region, model_list)
2) Runner authenticates with the control plane using the provided admin token and calls /health and /ready endpoints with exponential backoff (max 3 retries, 10s base)
3) If API is ready, runner posts a lightweight model load request for each model in model_list: create session, request model load, poll /models/{id}/status until 'ready' or timeout
4) Once model is ready, run a standard warmup prompt for each model to populate KV cache and verify token streaming path; measure p50/p95 latency and record token-generation rates
5) For concurrent cold-start test, spawn 3 parallel model load flows against different nodes (if multi-AZ) and capture memory/CPU metrics exposed by node exporter
6) Emit a JSON summary file to the artifact store and push Prometheus metrics via the pushgateway if direct scraping is not available

7) Exit 0 only when all mandatory checks pass; on non-fatal warnings, return exit code 0 but include 'warnings' section in result; on fatal failures return non-zero and include error reasons and links to logs.
implementation_notes: Runner is implemented as a minimal Go binary + small shell wrapper to keep image size < 60MB; uses net/http for probes and a tiny Prometheus client
Terraform module will expose: post_deploy_checks_enabled (bool), post_deploy_image (string), post_deploy_timeout (int seconds), artifact_bucket (string), allowed_models (list of model identifiers)
Make sure runner supports an 'offline' mode where it only performs API readiness and skips model load (useful for customers with locked-down images)
Use existing infra IAM roles and a short-lived presigned URL pattern for artifact uploads to avoid embedding long-lived credentials
Keep default timeouts conservative (total post-deploy timeout default 15m) and allow customers to extend via module var
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Post-deploy checks can lengthen terraform apply; Mitigation: default off and opt-in, allow async invocation with a polling status endpoint
Risk: Synthetic loads may surface false positives on transient infra glitches; Mitigation: include retry/backoff and require persistent failure across X attempts before reporting fatal
Risk: Runner could accidentally trigger customer model billing; Mitigation: use minimal warmup prompts and a dedicated 'verification' model list that avoids heavy generation
Risk: Secrets leakage via artifact store; Mitigation: scrub tokens from logs and use short-lived upload credentials
